title: Half-way between x and 1
caption: D^½ x = 2√(x/π) sits between f = x and its ordinary derivative 1: it is 2 at x = π. Applying the half-derivative again gives 1, so two half-steps make one whole derivative.
alt: Three graphs for x between 0 and 4: the line y = x, the square-root curve y = 2√(x/π) rising from 0, and the horizontal line y = 1.
description: f(x) = x is the line through the origin.
D^½ f = 2√(x/π) is the curve between them; at x = π it equals 2.
D^½ applied to that curve gives the constant 1 = f′.

checks.name: D^½ x = 2√(x/π) equals 2 at x = π
